avoid_when: never replace fixed evaluation
candidates.summary: Explains official and advisory metrics, their weighting, tradeoffs, and interpretation hazards.
candidates.title: Within-user ranking and diagnostic metrics
use_when: diagnosing every scored experiment
predicting metric-specific effects

avoid_when: Most training groups are homogeneous, because they yield no valid positive-negative pairs.
Cross-user negatives would be needed to create pairs; these are misaligned with within-user scoring.
Pair enumeration is too large and negative sampling cannot be made deterministic.
candidates.summary: Construct preference pairs only within the same displayed user candidate group, with a positive long-view impression preferred to a negative one, and optimize logistic score differences. Sample a bounded number of negatives per positive to control cost while directly training the ordering used by GAUC.
candidates.title: Within-user RankNet pairwise ranking loss
use_when: Validation GAUC is the limiting metric and mixed-label user groups are sufficiently common.
The model can batch impressions by user candidate group.
A ranking-focused alternative to pointwise BCE is required without listwise softmax instability.

avoid_when: The sole objective must explicitly prioritize top-five swaps and a stable pointwise baseline has already plateaued.
Labels are missing or are not available for every scored training impression.
candidates.summary: Train the long-view logit with numerically stable binary cross-entropy, weighting each impression inversely by its user candidate-count so prolific users do not dominate a GAUC-style within-user objective. Use this as the low-variance reference objective and preserve raw probabilities for diagnostics.
candidates.title: User-normalized pointwise binary cross-entropy
use_when: A reliable first neural-ranker objective is needed under scarce experiment budget.
The scorer needs a stable supervised signal on every labeled impression.
Candidate lists contain many zero/mixed/all-positive groups, making pure ranking losses partially undefined or uninformative.

avoid_when: Searching many unplanned slices until a favorable result appears
Ranking models by tiny slices with inadequate mixed-label groups
Using slices built from post-impression information unavailable at scoring time
candidates.summary: Decompose validation GAUC and nDCG@5 into predeclared slices: validation time block, user-history depth, user and video frequency bucket, candidate-group size, and zero-positive, mixed, or all-positive label composition. Report support and uncertainty beside each slice rather than selecting models from a single noisy subgroup.
candidates.title: Temporal and population-slice ranking dashboard
use_when: Checking whether an overall gain is robust across late validation time blocks
Diagnosing cold or sparse-entity failures
Selecting between models with similar aggregate metrics but different deployment risks

avoid_when: Using calibration metrics as a replacement for GAUC or nDCG@5 model selection
Fitting a calibrator on validation labels and then reporting that same validation result
Applying monotonic calibration solely to manufacture a ranking gain
candidates.summary: Supplement rank metrics with train-fitted calibration diagnostics such as Brier score, log loss, reliability bins, and predicted-positive-rate checks. Inspect errors separately for mixed candidate groups, because a model can preserve ranking while producing unstable probabilities that impair multitask weighting, threshold analyses, and ensemble averaging.
candidates.title: Probability calibration and ranking-error audit
use_when: Training with BCE or multitask binary heads
Averaging predictions or combining score heads
Investigating whether a ranking improvement came with implausibly extreme or collapsed probabilities

avoid_when: An auxiliary label leaks post-impression information into input features or is unavailable on validation.
Auxiliary-task weighting harms the primary GAUC or nDCG@5 in a fixed ablation.
The auxiliary behavior represents a conflicting preference rather than an earlier or related engagement signal.
required_features: one or more auxiliary outcome labels
candidates.summary: Attach lightweight binary heads for measured auxiliary engagement labels to the same ranker trunk, retain a dedicated long-view head for scoring, and optimize a weighted sum of user-normalized BCE losses. Keep long-view dominant; admit an auxiliary task only when its label is impression-time valid, sufficiently prevalent, and positively useful on validation.
candidates.title: Shared-trunk auxiliary-behavior multitask loss
use_when: The supplied log has auxiliary outcome labels with adequate support.
Long-view positives are sparse and the base model appears variance-limited.
Shared user, video, context, and history representations are already available.

avoid_when: The selected production candidate is a non-sequential MLP ranker.
History augmentation changes the meaning of the sequence, such as aggressively deleting rare but decisive recent events.
There is insufficient compute for a clearly separated pretraining and fine-tuning comparison.
candidates.summary: For a causal sequence encoder, pretrain user-history representations with two independently augmented views of the same strictly prior interaction sequence, then fine-tune on the supervised long-view ranking task. Use conservative history cropping, masking, and short subsequence views; never include interactions at or after the scored impression.
candidates.title: Causal sequence-view contrastive pretraining before ranking fine-tuning
use_when: Using the causal sequence-transformer ranker with enough historical events.
Sparse or short histories make supervised sequence training unstable.
The supervised sequence model underperforms simpler ID-plus-MLP models despite adequate optimization.

avoid_when: Candidate groups are predominantly size one or have no mixed labels.
The implementation cannot compute group-local ranks and swap deltas without leakage across groups.
Experiment budget cannot support a controlled coefficient comparison against the BCE parent.
required_features: candidate position only for training-group reconstruction
candidates.summary: Combine user-normalized binary cross-entropy with a within-user pairwise logistic term weighted by the absolute nDCG@5 change induced by swapping each positive-negative pair. Start with BCE-dominant weighting and tune one fixed ranking-loss coefficient, targeting top-five order without discarding broad GAUC supervision.
candidates.title: BCE plus LambdaRank-style nDCG@5 hybrid
use_when: nDCG@5 trails GAUC or top-ranked errors are the principal failure mode.
Candidate groups have at least some positive-negative pairs and usually exceed one candidate.
A compact metric-aligned change can be tested on top of an established BCE model.

avoid_when: The baseline is underfit or training is already compute-constrained.
Perturbation strength has not been bounded relative to typical embedding norms.
Using a highly brittle listwise implementation that cannot safely perform a second forward/backward pass.
candidates.summary: Add a small worst-case norm-bounded perturbation to learned user, video, and optional metadata embeddings during training, then optimize the ordinary ranking loss plus the perturbed-loss term. Start from a converged non-adversarial checkpoint and perturb only dense embedding representations, not raw IDs or causal aggregate inputs.
candidates.title: Adversarial perturbation regularization for embedding rankers
use_when: Embedding-based rankers overfit despite ordinary dropout and weight decay.
Validation performance is unstable across seeds or degrades sharply for sparse entities.
A robust regularization experiment is justified after a strong baseline exists.

avoid_when: Creating an auxiliary retrieval benchmark explicitly defined over a different full-catalog candidate universe
Treating sampled-negative metrics as interchangeable with the fixed official ranking metric
candidates.summary: Evaluate every model on the exact supplied displayed candidate groups and their canonical row order. Audit group completeness, duplicate rows, score coverage, label composition, and denominator handling before metric computation; never replace displayed candidates with sampled negatives for the official result.
candidates.title: Frozen displayed-candidate evaluation audit
use_when: Implementing official within-user GAUC or nDCG@5 scoring
Validating a newly generated prediction artifact
Comparing models whose dataloaders or ranking heads may reorder, drop, or duplicate impressions

avoid_when: Training a strictly pointwise-only baseline where group reconstruction materially limits throughput.
Candidate-group identifiers cannot be reconstructed reliably.
required_features: candidate order or stable impression identifier
candidates.summary: Build minibatches from complete displayed candidate groups rather than independent impressions. Stratify group sampling by zero-positive, mixed-label, and all-positive groups, while ensuring every mixed group retains all of its displayed candidates so pairwise and listwise losses see valid within-user comparisons.
candidates.title: Group-complete, label-stratified minibatching
use_when: Training RankNet, LambdaRank-style, or ListNet objectives.
The primary metrics are computed within user candidate groups.
Mixed-label groups are uncommon enough that ordinary row sampling yields many uninformative batches.

avoid_when: Most groups have only one item or homogeneous labels.
Group reconstruction is ambiguous or batch memory prevents complete groups.
A label-derived probability distribution would be dominated by unreliable graded or duplicated targets.
candidates.summary: For each mixed-label within-user candidate group, minimize cross-entropy between a label-derived top-one distribution and the softmax of model scores. Exclude zero-positive and all-positive groups from this term, then optionally retain a small BCE anchor so listwise normalization does not erase useful absolute-label supervision.
candidates.title: Mixed-group ListNet top-one loss
use_when: Displayed candidate groups are short and can be packed intact into batches.
The experiment seeks a genuinely listwise alternative to pairwise objectives.
Top-of-list competition among several simultaneously scored candidates is important.

avoid_when: Replacing the fixed official validation score with this audit without an approved protocol change
Mixing random and ordinary impressions into one unstratified metric
Claiming causal policy value when the available random log lacks the required policy and support information
candidates.summary: Keep official validation ranking as the model-selection target, then score a separately frozen random-exposure holdout as a secondary audit. Compare each model's ordinary-log and random-exposure ranking behavior, with matched support summaries, to detect gains likely tied to the historical exposure policy rather than user preference.
candidates.title: Random-exposure generalization audit
use_when: Assessing whether a model overfits recommendation-policy exposure patterns
Comparing popularity-heavy, causal-history, or debiased variants
Making a final robustness claim after official validation selection is complete

avoid_when: Most useful information is in the ordered item sequence rather than tabular field interactions.
Feature dimensions or categorical vocabularies are so sparse that extra cross capacity overfits despite regularization.
candidates.summary: Augment an embedding-plus-MLP scorer with a small Deep & Cross Network branch so that user, video, context, popularity, and history fields receive explicit bounded-degree crosses alongside nonlinear deep interactions.
candidates.title: Deep & Cross ranker for bounded-order feature interactions
use_when: Interactions such as user-by-category affinity, video-by-context, and recency-by-history-length are expected to matter.
You want controlled explicit crosses without enumerating manual feature conjunctions.
The embedding-plus-MLP baseline has useful signal but leaves room for better GAUC or nDCG@5.

avoid_when: Candidate-specific history attention or complex feature crosses have already shown a clear validated gain worth their added cost.
The target depends primarily on nonlinear context interactions that a shallow residual cannot recover.
required_features: impression-time context and numeric features; optional
candidates.summary: Use a compact user–video dot product as the main affinity score, then add a small linear or one-hidden-layer residual head for causal numeric, metadata, and context features. This provides a materially cheaper comparator to MLP and attention rankers while preserving personalized score variation.
candidates.title: Dot-product ranker with a small linear residual head
use_when: A fast, low-variance baseline is needed before spending scarce experiments on deeper rankers.
The deployment path may later require efficient batched scoring or approximate inner-product retrieval.
User and video ID embeddings carry substantial predictive signal.

avoid_when: The official split is effectively i.i.d. or temporal analysis shows no material drift.
The recent period is too small or label-sparse to support stronger weighting.
Timestamps, event ordering, or cutoff handling are ambiguous and could introduce future information.
candidates.summary: Apply a bounded exponential time-decay multiplier to complete training candidate groups, preserving within-group labels and user normalization while giving recent impressions more influence. Select only from a short predeclared half-life grid, normalize total training weight, and retain a nonzero minimum weight for older groups so the ranker adapts to preference or inventory drift without catastrophically forgetting sparse entities.
candidates.title: Recency-weighted causal ranking training
use_when: Chronological validation or the temporal slice dashboard indicates recent-period ranking degradation.
Timestamps are reliable and all recency weights are computed relative to the training cutoff, never future validation data.
The catalog, popularity distribution, or engagement behavior plausibly changes over the observation window.

avoid_when: The target is driven mainly by stable user-video affinity and histories are mostly sparse.
Event timestamps are tied or unreliable enough that causal ordering cannot be implemented safely.
Scarce experiment budget cannot support checking sequence length, dropout, and attention-width sensitivity.
candidates.summary: Encode each user's strictly pre-impression video sequence with a lightweight causal self-attention encoder, combine its last-state representation with the candidate video and context embeddings, and score the displayed impression with a shallow head.
candidates.title: Causal self-attentive sequence encoder ranker
use_when: Timestamp ordering is reliable and sequential transitions or evolving interests are likely to add signal beyond aggregates.
Users have enough prior interactions for sequence modeling after causal truncation.
You can cap history length and use a small transformer to keep training and inference practical.

avoid_when: Aggregate tables include the target row, future events, or validation/test outcomes.
Counts are treated as static when they are unavailable at the actual impression time.
The supplied aggregate-statistics table has unclear causal provenance.
required_features: video attributes or creator fields; use none when unavailable
candidates.summary: Add smoothed, causally available counts and rates for videos, creators or categories, plus user-by-attribute affinities, fitted on training prefixes and backed off for sparse groups.
candidates.title: Train-prefix smoothed popularity and affinity statistics
use_when: IDs and metadata are sparse enough that aggregate evidence can complement embeddings.
The pipeline can enforce train-only fitting and timestamp-prefix lookup.
Rare-item estimates can be shrunk toward global or attribute-level priors.

avoid_when: Neither propensity nor outcome nuisance models can be validated independently.
The random-exposure data has negligible coverage of important users, videos, or contexts, making nuisance-model extrapolation dominant.
Implementation cannot enforce fold separation or train-only fitting for imputation and propensity models.
required_features: exposure propensity or train-fitted propensity estimate
imputation-model inputs restricted to impression-time availability
fold or temporal split identifier for nuisance-model isolation
candidates.summary: Combine a direct long-view outcome model with a propensity-corrected residual loss: train the ranking model on an imputed outcome term plus a clipped IPS correction for observed-label errors. Cross-fit or isolate nuisance-model fitting from scored folds, keep the final scorer group-aware, and compare against both ordinary and IPS-only objectives to determine whether the imputation model reduces high-variance propensity correction.
candidates.title: Doubly robust exposure-debiased ranking objective
use_when: Propensities pass overlap checks but IPS-only training is noisy or sensitive to reasonable clipping levels.
There is adequate training support to fit both an outcome/imputation model and a propensity model using only pre-impression information.
The experiment budget supports a clearly predeclared three-way test: ordinary baseline, IPS, and doubly robust.

avoid_when: The validation result shows that a candidate-specific reading of behavioral history is consistently valuable.
A simple model already saturates both GAUC and nDCG@5 and scarce experiments are better spent on objective or feature changes.
candidates.summary: A compact pointwise scorer that concatenates user/video ID embeddings, metadata embeddings, causal history features, and numeric aggregates before a residual MLP outputs one long-view logit per impression.
candidates.title: Embedding-plus-MLP pointwise ranker
use_when: A strong, low-risk architecture baseline is needed before adding specialized interaction or sequence modules.
Candidate lists are short and scoring every displayed impression independently is computationally inexpensive.
You need an architecture that cleanly accommodates all causally available dense and categorical features.

avoid_when: The dataset is small enough that quantization adds engineering risk without a meaningful resource benefit.
Low-precision kernels are unavailable or prediction parity cannot be verified on the target hardware.
Rare-entity ranking quality is a primary concern and dequantization error is concentrated in those rows.
candidates.summary: Keep infrequent embedding rows in low precision and retain a bounded full-precision cache for the most frequently accessed training entities. Use per-row scale metadata, a deterministic cache rule based only on training frequencies, and verify score drift before accepting the memory reduction.
candidates.title: Quantized embedding tables with a full-precision hot-row cache
use_when: Embedding-table and optimizer-state memory limits batch size, model width, or feasible architecture choices.
Frequent entities dominate accesses and a compact deployment artifact is required.
The runtime supports tested low-precision embedding lookup on the intended Windows/Linux target.

avoid_when: Short-budget rankings are known to be unstable, especially for sequence models or delayed auxiliary-task gains.
The low-fidelity rung changes candidate-group composition, leakage handling, or the official evaluation definition.
The protocol prohibits adaptive allocation of experiment budget across candidates.
candidates.summary: Screen predeclared configurations using a deterministic low-cost rung, promote only the best few by a fixed composite ranking rule, and rerun promoted candidates at full training fidelity and full frozen validation scoring. Log every rung, seed, budget, and promotion decision to conserve counted experiments without silently changing selection criteria.
candidates.title: Predeclared successive-halving experiment promotion
use_when: Official experiments are scarce and several credible architecture, objective, or regularization variants compete.
Early epochs or a fixed validation subset have empirically useful rank correlation with full-fidelity results.
The configuration grid and promotion thresholds can be fixed before running trials.

avoid_when: Each row genuinely has distinct user-side context or a distinct causal cutoff that prevents safe sharing.
The implementation cannot prove that grouped vectorization preserves canonical row order and identical numerical outputs.
candidates.summary: Compute candidate-invariant inputs once per displayed candidate group: user embedding, causal history encoder output, user metadata transforms, and group-level numeric features. Broadcast that state across candidate videos and score the complete group in one vectorized call, preserving scores exactly while reducing repeated work.
candidates.title: Candidate-group shared representation scoring
use_when: Using causal history attention or a sequence encoder for multiple videos shown to the same user at one impression.
Candidate groups are evaluated intact and contain repeated user-side inputs.
CPU or GPU prediction time is a practical constraint.

avoid_when: IDs are unavailable at scoring time.
Most validation entities are unseen and no side information is available for fallback.
candidates.summary: Use compact learned embeddings for user and video IDs as the primary personalization signal, with explicit unknown-index handling and frequency-aware regularization for rare entities.
candidates.title: User and video identity embeddings with cold/OOV handling
use_when: The validation set contains mostly warm users or videos seen during training.
A simple personalized baseline is needed before adding side features or histories.
Candidate lists require within-user score variation.
